alex: Quick sanity-check thread — ran the slot allocator A/B where A = skiplist-backed slot map and B = buddy allocator with 8/16/32b block buckets. Observed weird tail growth on B when serving long-context streams (~50k tokens).

mike: Can you paste the short perf snapshot?

alex: Sure — gist of results from a 6h load test (same request mix):
- skiplist (A): steady mem +3.8% p50 over baseline, 1.1% p95 spikes
- buddy (B): steady mem +12.4% p50, p95 spikes to +28% and saw intermittent OOM on small worker pools
- compaction passes triggered: A did background coalesce every 15m w/o stalls, B's compaction took 120-350ms pauses and often skipped small holes

sarah: interesting. did you capture hole distribution? is B creating lots of microholes <64B?

alex: yes — exported `kv_cache_dump --histogram` and this was the bucket breakdown (top lines):
```
small_holes(<64B): 71.2%
medium(64-512B): 18.7%
large(>512B): 10.1%
```
B ended up with many tiny free slots inside larger blocks because buddy splits but doesn't re-coalesce across reuse patterns; skiplist allows more precise reuse.

jordan: Did you try tuning the buddy min-block to 32 -> 64 transition? might reduce microhole count but increase internal fragmentation.

alex: I did a quick sweep: moving base bucket from 32->64 reduced microholes to 43% but increased baseline allocation pressure (more bytes reserved) so latency slightly improved but cost went up ~7% in tokens/sec equivalence.

lina: Any evidence of sticky KV entries (long-lived keys) causing slab warming and preventing compaction?

alex: Good call — trace shows ~8% of keys become "sticky" after long-context sessions (they pin KV frames because of incremental attention windows). Those pins prevent compaction merging on B because buddy expects contiguous free buddies. Skiplist can reassign small freed extents more flexibly.

mike: Is there a quick mitigation we can ship to reduce OOM risk on B without swapping allocator?

alex: Proposal: add a light-weight scavenger that opportunistically remaps small freed extents into a mini free-cache for immediate reuse (no full coalesce), plus a background async coalesce pass that runs per-N allocations when server Q < 30%. Implementation sketch:
```
- per-shard mini_cache: a lock-free freelist of small holes (<128B)
- on alloc: check mini_cache first, then normal buddy alloc
- background_coalesce: T=30s, only run when load low; do merge of adjacent free buddies
```
Pros: low-latency reuse, minimal change to buddy core. Cons: added code paths + extra memory for mini_cache.

jordan: Sounds reasonable. Could we instrument a metric for "microhole reclaim rate" and a gauge for mini_cache hits so we can measure before/after?

alex: Yup — plan to add these: `kv.microhole_hits`, `kv.microhole_misses`, `kv.coalesce_cycles`, and `kv.sticky_key_fraction`.

dev-bot: perf-ci build/3372 started for alex/kv-mini-cache-proto :rocket:

sarah: Also let's add a test that simulates long-context churn (50k tokens) with pinned keys and verify p95 mem growth stays <8% over 6h. If proto passes we can A/B rollout.

mike: +1 on metrics + test. once we have data we can decide whether to keep buddy or flip to skiplist in hot-paths. :eyes:

alex: I'll push a draft PR with the mini_cache impl and instrumentation. If you want to reproduce locally:
```
# synthetic load harness
./tools/kv_stress --mode=longstream --clients=40 --tokens=50000 --pin-prob=0.08 --report-interval=60
# perf helper
perf record -o perf.data -F 99 -a -- ./bin/redisish --kv-backend=buddy
perf script -i perf.data | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg
```

lina: thanks — ping when PR ready, will try on a small dedicated pool. :+1:

alex: will do. tl;dr: buddy is cheaper in avg allocation but suffers microhole accumulation under long-context pinned keys; mini_cache + background coalesce is low-risk mitigation to reduce OOM/regressions.

mike: nice analysis, alex. good next steps.
